topics.title: Quadratic functions — factoring and the graph

questions.stem: Consider the concave-up parabola with equation \( y = (x - 2)(x - 4) \). Explain why the parabola is concave up.
options: The constant term is positive (\( c = 8 > 0 \)).
The parabola has two distinct real roots.
The coefficient of \( x^2 \) is positive (\( a = 1 > 0 \)).
The coefficient of \( x^2 \) is negative (\( a = -1 < 0 \)).
questions.hint: Look at the sign of the coefficient of the \( x^2 \) term when expanded.
questions.solution: When expanded, the equation is \( y = x^2 - 6x + 8 \). The leading coefficient of the quadratic term \( x^2 \) is \( a = 1 \), which is positive. This means the parabola is concave up.

steps.explain: Expand the factored form equation to find the general form.
Identify the leading coefficient a of the quadratic term.
Since the coefficient is positive, the parabola opens upwards.

questions.stem: Find the \( y \)-intercept of the parabola with equation \( y = (x - 2)(x - 4) \).
questions.hint: Substitute \( x = 0 \) into the equation.
questions.solution: To find the vertical intercept, substitute \( x = 0 \): \( y = (0 - 2)(0 - 4) = (-2) \times (-4) = 8 \). Thus, the vertical intercept is at \( (0, 8) \).

steps.explain: Substitute x = 0 into the function rule.
Multiply the factors together to find the value of y.

questions.stem: Find the \( x \)-intercepts of the parabola with equation \( y = (x - 2)(x - 4) \).
questions.hint: Set \( y = 0 \) and apply the null factor law.
questions.solution: Set \( y = 0 \) to find the horizontal intercepts: \( (x - 2)(x - 4) = 0 \). By the null factor law, \( x = 2 \) or \( x = 4 \).

steps.explain: Set the equation equal to zero.
Apply the null factor law to solve for the x-intercepts.

questions.stem: Determine the equation of the axis of symmetry for the parabola \( y = (x - 2)(x - 4) \).
questions.hint: The axis of symmetry lies exactly halfway between the horizontal intercepts.
questions.solution: The horizontal intercepts are at \( x = 2 \) and \( x = 4 \). The axis of symmetry is the average of these intercepts: \( x = \dfrac{2 + 4}{2} = 3 \).

steps.explain: Find the average of the two intercepts.

questions.stem: Determine the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola \( y = (x - 2)(x - 4) \).
questions.hint: Substitute the x-value of the axis of symmetry back into the equation.
questions.solution: The axis of symmetry is \( x = 3 \). Substituting this into the function gives: \( y = (3 - 2)(3 - 4) = 1 \times (-1) = -1 \). So the vertex is at \( (3, -1) \).

steps.explain: Substitute the axis of symmetry value x = 3 into the function.
Evaluate the expression to find the y-value of the vertex.

questions.stem: Does the quadratic function \( y = (x - 2)(x - 4) \) have equal zeroes or distinct zeroes?
questions.hint: Look at the values of the horizontal intercepts.
questions.solution: The zeroes of the function are \( x = 2 \) and \( x = 4 \). Since these two numbers are different, the zeroes are distinct.

steps.explain: Identify the zeroes of the function.
Compare the zeroes to determine if they are distinct.

questions.stem: For the parabola with equation \( y = -x(x - 4) \), explain why the graph is concave down.
options: The vertex lies in the first quadrant.
The coefficient of \( x^2 \) is negative (\( a = -1 < 0 \)).
The coefficient of \( x^2 \) is positive (\( a = 1 > 0 \)).
questions.hint: Determine the leading coefficient after expanding the function.
questions.solution: Expanding \( y = -x(x-4) \) yields \( y = -x^2 + 4x \). The coefficient of the quadratic term \( x^2 \) is \( a = -1 \). Since this is negative, the parabola is concave down.

steps.explain: Expand the factored equation.
Identify the leading coefficient and check its sign.

questions.stem: Find the \( y \)-intercept of the parabola with equation \( y = -x(x - 4) \).
questions.hint: Substitute \( x = 0 \) into the equation.
questions.solution: Substitute \( x = 0 \) into the function: \( y = -0(0 - 4) = 0 \). The vertical intercept is at the origin, \( (0, 0) \).

steps.explain: Substitute x = 0 into the function equation.

questions.stem: Find the \( x \)-intercepts of the parabola with equation \( y = -x(x - 4) \).
questions.hint: Set the equation equal to zero and apply the null factor law.
questions.solution: Setting \( y = 0 \) gives \( -x(x - 4) = 0 \). Using the null factor law, \( x = 0 \) or \( x = 4 \).

steps.explain: Set y = 0.
Solve for x.

questions.stem: Determine the equation of the axis of symmetry for the parabola \( y = -x(x - 4) \).
questions.hint: Calculate the average of the horizontal intercepts.
questions.solution: The intercepts are at \( x = 0 \) and \( x = 4 \). The midpoint is \( x = \dfrac{0 + 4}{2} = 2 \).

steps.explain: Find the midpoint between 0 and 4.

questions.stem: Find the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola \( y = -x(x - 4) \).
questions.hint: Substitute the axis of symmetry x = 2 back into the equation.
questions.solution: Substitute \( x = 2 \) into the equation: \( y = -2(2 - 4) = -2 \times (-2) = 4 \). The vertex is at \( (2, 4) \).

steps.explain: Substitute x = 2 into the function formula.
Simplify to find the vertical coordinate.

questions.stem: Does the quadratic function \( y = -x(x - 4) \) have equal zeroes or distinct zeroes?
questions.hint: Compare the zeroes of the function.
questions.solution: The zeroes are \( x = 0 \) and \( x = 4 \). Since they are distinct values, the function has two distinct zeroes.

steps.explain: Identify and compare the zeroes.

questions.stem: For the perfect square parabola with equation \( y = (x - 3)^2 \), explain its concavity.
options: Concave down because it is a perfect square.
Concave up because the vertex is at (3, 0).
Concave up because the coefficient of \( x^2 \) is positive (\( a = 1 > 0 \)).
Concave down because the coefficient of \( x^2 \) is negative (\( a = -1 < 0 \)).
questions.hint: Look at the leading coefficient after expanding the perfect square.
questions.solution: Expanding \( y = (x-3)^2 \) yields \( y = x^2 - 6x + 9 \). The leading coefficient is \( a = 1 \), which is positive. Therefore, the parabola is concave up.

steps.explain: Expand the perfect square expression.
Verify that the leading coefficient is positive.

questions.stem: Find the \( y \)-intercept of the parabola with equation \( y = (x - 3)^2 \).
questions.hint: Substitute \( x = 0 \) into the equation.
questions.solution: Substitute \( x = 0 \): \( y = (0 - 3)^2 = (-3)^2 = 9 \). The vertical intercept is at \( (0, 9) \).

steps.explain: Substitute x = 0.

questions.stem: Find the single \( x \)-intercept of the perfect square parabola \( y = (x - 3)^2 \).
questions.hint: Set \( y = 0 \) and solve.
questions.solution: Set \( y = 0 \) to find the horizontal intercept: \( (x - 3)^2 = 0 \implies x - 3 = 0 \implies x = 3 \). This is a single, repeated root.

steps.explain: Set the function to zero.
Take the square root and solve.

questions.stem: For the parabola with equation \( y = (x - 3)^2 \), use symmetry about \( x = 3 \) and the vertical intercept \( (0, 9) \) to find another point on the parabola.
questions.hint: The axis of symmetry is \( x = 3 \). A point 3 units to the left has a height of 9. Find the coordinates of the point 3 units to the right.
questions.solution: The axis of symmetry is at \( x = 3 \). The point \( (0, 9) \) is 3 units to the left of the axis of symmetry. Symmetrically, another point with the same y-value of 9 must exist 3 units to the right of the axis of symmetry, at \( x = 3 + 3 = 6 \). This point is \( (6, 9) \).

steps.explain: Analyze distance from axis of symmetry.
Reflect the point across the axis of symmetry.

questions.stem: Does the quadratic function \( y = (x - 3)^2 \) have equal zeroes or distinct zeroes?
questions.hint: Check how many times the graph touches the x-axis.
questions.solution: The equation \( y = (x - 3)^2 \) has a single repeated root at \( x = 3 \). Since the roots are the same, it has equal zeroes.

steps.explain: Solve for the zeroes.
Conclude that the roots are equal.

questions.stem: For the parabola with equation \( y = \dfrac{1}{4}x^2 \), find the value of \( y \) when \( x = 4 \).
questions.hint: Substitute \( x = 4 \) into the equation.
questions.solution: Substitute \( x = 4 \) into the function rule: \( y = \dfrac{1}{4}(4)^2 = \dfrac{1}{4} \times 16 = 4 \).

steps.explain: Substitute x = 4 into the equation.
Evaluate the power and simplify.

questions.stem: Since \( y = \dfrac{1}{4}x^2 \) passes through \( (4, 4) \), what other point must lie on the parabola due to symmetry about the \( y \)-axis?
questions.hint: Reflect the point \( (4, 4) \) across the line \( x = 0 \).
questions.solution: The axis of symmetry is the y-axis (\( x = 0 \)). Reflecting the point \( (4, 4) \) across the y-axis yields the point \( (-4, 4) \).

steps.explain: Reflect the point across the line x = 0.

questions.stem: Write down, in factored form, the equation of the monic quadratic function with zeroes \( x = 3 \) and \( x = 5 \).
questions.hint: A zero at \( x = k \) corresponds to a factor of \( (x - k) \).
questions.solution: The zeroes are \( 3 \) and \( 5 \), so the factors are \( (x - 3) \) and \( (x - 5) \). Since the quadratic is monic, the coefficient of the product is 1: \( y = (x - 3)(x - 5) \).

steps.explain: Determine factors from the given zeroes.
Combine the factors with leading coefficient 1.

questions.stem: Write down, in factored form, the equation of the monic quadratic function with zeroes \( x = 0 \) and \( x = 4 \).
questions.hint: Use the factors \( (x - 0) \) and \( (x - 4) \).
questions.solution: The zeroes are \( 0 \) and \( 4 \). The factors are \( (x - 0) = x \) and \( (x - 4) \). The monic equation is \( y = x(x - 4) \).

steps.explain: Identify the factors.
Combine to form the equation.

questions.stem: Write down, in factored form, the equation of the monic quadratic function with zeroes \( x = -2 \) and \( x = 6 \).
questions.hint: Subtract each zero from \( x \) to form the factors.
questions.solution: Zeroes are \( -2 \) and \( 6 \). The factors are \( (x - (-2)) = (x + 2) \) and \( (x - 6) \). The equation is \( y = (x + 2)(x - 6) \).

steps.explain: Create factors, taking care of negative values.
Multiply factors to get the monic function.

questions.stem: Write down, in factored form, the equation of the monic quadratic function with zeroes \( x = -5 \) and \( x = -2 \).
questions.hint: Subtract negative zeroes from \( x \).
questions.solution: The zeroes are \( -5 \) and \( -2 \). The factors are \( (x - (-5)) = (x + 5) \) and \( (x - (-2)) = (x + 2) \). The monic quadratic is \( y = (x + 5)(x + 2) \).

steps.explain: Determine factors from negative zeroes.
Form the equation.

questions.stem: A parabola is concave up and has \( x \)-intercepts at \( x = 0 \) and \( x = 4 \). What is the equation in factored form?
questions.hint: Concave up means the leading coefficient is positive.
questions.solution: With intercepts at 0 and 4, the factors are \( x \) and \( (x - 4) \). Since the parabola is concave up, the leading coefficient is positive: \( y = x(x - 4) \).

steps.explain: Identify factors from intercepts.
Choose positive sign for concave up.

questions.stem: A parabola is concave up and has \( x \)-intercepts at \( x = -3 \) and \( x = 2 \). What is the equation in factored form?
questions.hint: Setup factors for \( x = -3 \) and \( x = 2 \) and use a positive sign.
questions.solution: The zeroes are \( -3 \) and \( 2 \). The factors are \( (x + 3) \) and \( (x - 2) \). For a concave-up parabola, the leading coefficient is positive: \( y = (x + 3)(x - 2) \).

steps.explain: Form the factors.
Combine them for a concave-up parabola.

questions.stem: A parabola is concave down and has \( x \)-intercepts at \( x = -2 \) and \( x = 4 \). What is the equation in factored form?
questions.hint: Concave down means the leading coefficient is negative.
questions.solution: The zeroes are \( -2 \) and \( 4 \). The factors are \( (x + 2) \) and \( (x - 4) \). Since the parabola is concave down, we add a negative sign: \( y = -(x + 2)(x - 4) \).

steps.explain: Identify factors from zeroes.
Combine factors with negative coefficient for concave down.

questions.stem: A parabola is concave down and has \( x \)-intercepts at \( x = -6 \) and \( x = -1 \). What is the equation in factored form?
questions.hint: Set up factors for negative zeroes and add a negative leading sign.
questions.solution: The zeroes are \( -6 \) and \( -1 \). The factors are \( (x + 6) \) and \( (x + 1) \). As it is concave down, the equation is \( y = -(x + 6)(x + 1) \).

questions.stem: Determine the zeroes and the coordinates of the vertex for the quadratic function \( f(x) = x^2 - 16 \).
questions.hint: Use difference of two squares to factorize the equation.
questions.solution: Factorize using the difference of two squares: \( f(x) = (x - 4)(x + 4) \). Setting \( f(x) = 0 \) yields zeroes at \( x = -4 \) and \( x = 4 \). The axis of symmetry is \( x = 0 \). Substituting \( x = 0 \) gives the vertex at \( (0, -16) \).

steps.explain: Factorize the expression using the difference of squares formula.

questions.stem: Find the zeroes and the coordinates of the vertex for the quadratic function \( f(x) = x^2 + 2x - 3 \).
questions.hint: Find two numbers that multiply to -3 and add to 2 to factor the quadratic.
questions.solution: Factorize: \( f(x) = (x + 3)(x - 1) \). This gives zeroes at \( x = -3 \) and \( x = 1 \). The axis of symmetry is \( x = \dfrac{-3 + 1}{2} = -1 \). Substitute \( x = -1 \) to find the vertex: \( y = (-1)^2 + 2(-1) - 3 = 1 - 2 - 3 = -4 \). So the vertex is at \( (-1, -4) \).

steps.explain: Factorize the quadratic expression.
Solve for the zeroes.
Find the vertex coordinates.

questions.stem: Find the zeroes and the coordinates of the vertex for the quadratic function \( f(x) = x^2 + 2x - 8 \).
questions.hint: Find two numbers that multiply to -8 and add to 2.
questions.solution: Factorize: \( f(x) = (x + 4)(x - 2) \), giving zeroes at \( x = -4 \) and \( x = 2 \). The axis of symmetry is \( x = \dfrac{-4 + 2}{2} = -1 \). Substitute \( x = -1 \): \( y = (-1 + 4)(-1 - 2) = 3 \times (-3) = -9 \). The vertex is \( (-1, -9) \).

steps.explain: Factorize the quadratic.
Solve for the zeroes.
Find the axis of symmetry and vertex.

questions.stem: Determine the zeroes and the coordinates of the vertex for the quadratic function \( f(x) = 6x - x^2 \).
questions.hint: Factor out the common factor of x.
questions.solution: Factor: \( f(x) = x(6 - x) \). The zeroes are \( x = 0 \) and \( x = 6 \). Symmetrically, the vertex is at \( x = 3 \). Substituting \( x = 3 \) gives \( y = 6(3) - 3^2 = 18 - 9 = 9 \). The vertex is \( (3, 9) \).

questions.stem: Find the vertex (the single horizontal intercept) and the vertical intercept for the parabola \( y = x^2 - 4x + 4 \).
questions.hint: Express the quadratic as a perfect square.
questions.solution: Factorize as a perfect square: \( y = (x - 2)^2 \). The vertex (and single x-intercept) is at \( (2, 0) \). Substitute \( x = 0 \) to find the y-intercept: \( y = 4 \), so \( (0, 4) \).

questions.stem: Find the vertex (the single horizontal intercept) and the vertical intercept for the parabola \( y = -x^2 + 6x - 9 \).
questions.hint: Factor out -1 to recognize the perfect square form.
questions.solution: Factor: \( y = -(x^2 - 6x + 9) = -(x - 3)^2 \). The vertex is at \( (3, 0) \). Substitute \( x = 0 \) to get the y-intercept: \( y = -9 \), so \( (0, -9) \).

questions.stem: Find the \( x \)-intercepts and the \( y \)-intercept of the non-monic quadratic function \( y = 2x^2 + 9x + 4 \).
questions.hint: Factor by grouping to solve \( 2x^2 + 9x + 4 = 0 \).
questions.solution: Factor the quadratic: \( 2x^2 + 9x + 4 = 2x^2 + 8x + x + 4 = 2x(x + 4) + 1(x + 4) = (2x + 1)(x + 4) \).\nSetting to zero gives zeroes at \( x = -\dfrac{1}{2} \) and \( x = -4 \). Substitute \( x = 0 \) to find the y-intercept: \( y = 4 \).

questions.stem: Find the \( x \)-intercepts and the \( y \)-intercept of the non-monic quadratic function \( y = 2x^2 + 3x - 5 \).
questions.hint: Factor by grouping: look for numbers that multiply to -10 and add to 3.
questions.solution: Factor: \( 2x^2 + 3x - 5 = 2x^2 + 5x - 2x - 5 = x(2x + 5) - 1(2x + 5) = (2x + 5)(x - 1) \). zeroes: \( x = -\dfrac{5}{2} \) and \( x = 1 \). Substitute \( x = 0 \) to find y-intercept: \( y = -5 \).

questions.stem: Find the \( x \)-intercepts and the \( y \)-intercept of the non-monic quadratic function \( y = 3x^2 + 4x - 4 \).
questions.hint: Factor the expression: product is -12, sum is 4.
questions.solution: Factor: \( 3x^2 + 4x - 4 = 3x^2 + 6x - 2x - 4 = 3x(x + 2) - 2(x + 2) = (3x - 2)(x + 2) \). Zeroes: \( x = \dfrac{2}{3} \) and \( x = -2 \). Substitute \( x = 0 \) to find y-intercept: \( y = -4 \).

questions.stem: A parabola is concave up, has \( x \)-intercepts at \( x = -2 \) and \( x = 3 \), and a \( y \)-intercept at \( -6 \). Find its equation in factored form.
questions.hint: Write the general form \( y = a(x + 2)(x - 3) \) and find \( a \) using the y-intercept.
questions.solution: Using the intercepts, the general form is \( y = a(x + 2)(x - 3) \). The vertical intercept is at \( (0, -6) \). Substitute \( x = 0, y = -6 \):\n\( -6 = a(0 + 2)(0 - 3) \implies -6 = -6a \implies a = 1 \). Therefore, the equation is \( y = (x + 2)(x - 3) \).

questions.stem: A parabola is concave down, has \( x \)-intercepts at \( x = -4 \) and \( x = 2 \), and a \( y \)-intercept at \( 8 \). Find its equation in factored form.
questions.hint: Substitute \( (0, 8) \) into \( y = a(x + 4)(x - 2) \).
questions.solution: The general form is \( y = a(x + 4)(x - 2) \). Substituting the vertical intercept \( (0, 8) \):\n\( 8 = a(0 + 4)(0 - 2) \implies 8 = -8a \implies a = -1 \). Thus, the equation is \( y = -(x + 4)(x - 2) \).

questions.stem: A parabola is concave up, has \( x \)-intercepts at \( x = -3 \) and \( x = 3 \), and a \( y \)-intercept at \( -18 \). Find its equation in factored form.
questions.hint: Set up \( y = a(x + 3)(x - 3) \) and solve using the point \( (0, -18) \).
questions.solution: The general form is \( y = a(x + 3)(x - 3) \). Substitute \( (0, -18) \):\n\( -18 = a(0 + 3)(0 - 3) \implies -18 = -9a \implies a = 2 \). So the equation is \( y = 2(x + 3)(x - 3) \).

questions.stem: A parabola is concave down, has \( x \)-intercepts at \( x = -3 \) and \( x = 3 \), and a \( y \)-intercept at \( 3 \). Find its equation in factored form.
questions.hint: Use the general factored form and solve for \( a \) using the intercept \( (0, 3) \).
questions.solution: The general equation is \( y = a(x + 3)(x - 3) \). Substitute \( (0, 3) \):\n\( 3 = a(0 + 3)(0 - 3) \implies 3 = -9a \implies a = -\dfrac{1}{3} \). The equation is \( y = -\dfrac{1}{3}(x + 3)(x - 3) \).

questions.solution: Factored form: \( y = a(x - 2)(x - 4) \). Substitute \( (0, 16) \):\n\( 16 = a(0 - 2)(0 - 4) \implies 16 = 8a \implies a = 2 \). The equation is \( y = 2(x - 2)(x - 4) \).

questions.stem: Identify the two points through which all four parabolas from the family \( y = a(x - 2)(x - 4) \) pass, regardless of the value of \( a \).
questions.hint: Think about what values of x make \( y = 0 \) regardless of what \( a \) is.
questions.solution: The equation is \( y = a(x - 2)(x - 4) \). If we substitute the horizontal intercepts \( x = 2 \) or \( x = 4 \), the product becomes zero, meaning \( y = 0 \) regardless of \( a \). Therefore, all curves in this family pass through \( (2, 0) \) and \( (4, 0) \).

questions.stem: Find the zeroes and the coordinates of the vertex for the quadratic function \( y = 3x^2 - 12 \).
questions.hint: Factor out the common factor 3, then use difference of squares.
questions.solution: Factor out 3: \( y = 3(x^2 - 4) = 3(x - 2)(x + 2) \). Zeroes are at \( x = 2 \) and \( x = -2 \). The vertex is on the axis of symmetry \( x = 0 \). Substituting \( x = 0 \) yields \( y = -12 \). The vertex is \( (0, -12) \).

questions.stem: Find the zeroes and the coordinates of the vertex for the quadratic function \( y = 2x^2 + x - 3 \).
questions.hint: Factor the quadratic by grouping: product is -6, sum is 1.
questions.solution: Factor: \( 2x^2 + x - 3 = 2x^2 + 3x - 2x - 3 = x(2x + 3) - 1(2x + 3) = (2x + 3)(x - 1) \). Zeroes are \( x = -\dfrac{3}{2} \) and \( x = 1 \). Axis of symmetry is the midpoint: \( x = -\dfrac{1}{4} \). Vertex y-value: \( y = 2\left(-\dfrac{1}{4}\right)^2 + \left(-\dfrac{1}{4}\right) - 3 = \dfrac{2}{16} - \dfrac{1}{4} - 3 = -\dfrac{25}{8} \). The vertex is \( \left(-\dfrac{1}{4}, -\dfrac{25}{8}\right) \).

questions.stem: Find the zeroes and the coordinates of the vertex for the quadratic function \( y = 5x - 2 - 3x^2 \).
questions.hint: Rewrite the equation as \( -(3x^2 - 5x + 2) \) and factorize.
questions.solution: Rewrite and factor out -1: \( y = -(3x^2 - 5x + 2) = -(3x - 2)(x - 1) \). Zeroes are at \( x = \dfrac{2}{3} \) and \( x = 1 \). Axis of symmetry: \( x = \dfrac{5}{6} \). Vertex y-value: \( y = 5\left(\dfrac{5}{6}\right) - 2 - 3\left(\dfrac{5}{6}\right)^2 = \dfrac{25}{6} - 2 - \dfrac{75}{36} = \dfrac{1}{12} \). Vertex is \( \left(\dfrac{5}{6}, \dfrac{1}{12}\right) \).

questions.stem: The general form of a quadratic with zeroes \( x = 3 \) and \( x = 9 \) is \( y = a(x - 3)(x - 9) \). Find the equation of the parabola where the coefficient of \( x^2 \) is 2.
questions.hint: The coefficient of \( x^2 \) in the general form expansion is the parameter \( a \).
questions.solution: The general form is \( y = a(x - 3)(x - 9) \). Expanding this gives \( y = a(x^2 - 12x + 27) \). The coefficient of \( x^2 \) is \( a \). Since the coefficient must be 2, we have \( a = 2 \). The equation is \( y = 2(x - 3)(x - 9) \).

questions.stem: The general form of a quadratic with zeroes \( x = 3 \) and \( x = 9 \) is \( y = a(x - 3)(x - 9) \). Find the equation of the parabola where the \( y \)-intercept is \( -54 \).

questions.solution: The general form is \( y = a(x - 3)(x - 9) \). Substitute the vertical intercept \( (0, -54) \):\n\( -54 = a(0 - 3)(0 - 9) \implies -54 = 27a \implies a = -2 \). Thus, the equation is \( y = -2(x - 3)(x - 9) \).

questions.stem: The general form of a quadratic with zeroes \( x = 3 \) and \( x = 9 \) is \( y = a(x - 3)(x - 9) \). Find the equation of the parabola where the vertex is \( (6, -18) \).
questions.hint: Substitute the vertex coordinates \( (6, -18) \) into the general equation.
questions.solution: Substitute \( x = 6 \) and \( y = -18 \) into the general equation \( y = a(x - 3)(x - 9) \):\n\( -18 = a(6 - 3)(6 - 9) \implies -18 = a(3)(-3) \implies -18 = -9a \implies a = 2 \). The equation is \( y = 2(x - 3)(x - 9) \).

questions.stem: The general form of a quadratic with zeroes \( x = 3 \) and \( x = 9 \) is \( y = a(x - 3)(x - 9) \). Find the equation of the parabola which passes through \( (2, -14) \).

questions.solution: Substitute \( x = 2 \) and \( y = -14 \) into \( y = a(x - 3)(x - 9) \):\n\( -14 = a(2 - 3)(2 - 9) \implies -14 = a(-1)(-7) \implies -14 = 7a \implies a = -2 \). The equation is \( y = -2(x - 3)(x - 9) \).

parts.stem: a) Sketch the graph of \( y = (x + 2)^2 - 5 \), showing its vertex, y-intercept, and exact x-intercepts.
parts.answer: Parabola concave up with vertex (-2, -5), y-intercept (0, -1), and x-intercepts at -2 ± √5.

parts.stem: b) Sketch the graph of \( y = (x - 3)^2 - 6 \), showing its vertex, y-intercept, and exact x-intercepts.
parts.answer: Parabola concave up with vertex (3, -6), y-intercept (0, 3), and x-intercepts at 3 ± √6.

parts.stem: c) Sketch the graph of \( y = (x - 2)^2 - 3 \), showing its vertex, y-intercept, and exact x-intercepts.
parts.answer: Parabola concave up with vertex (2, -3), y-intercept (0, 1), and x-intercepts at 2 ± √3.

steps.explain: For part a, identify the vertex: \( V(-2, -5) \). Calculate y-intercept: \( y = (0+2)^2 - 5 = -1 \). Find x-intercepts: \( (x+2)^2 = 5 \implies x = -2 \pm \sqrt{5} \).
For part b, identify the vertex: \( V(3, -6) \). Calculate y-intercept: \( y = (0-3)^2 - 6 = 3 \). Find x-intercepts: \( (x-3)^2 = 6 \implies x = 3 \pm \sqrt{6} \).

questions.stem: Investigate properties of the family of parabolas given by \( y = a(x - 2)^2 - 3 \).

parts.stem: a) Sketch on a single coordinate plane the four parabolas corresponding to: \( a = 2 \), \( a = 1 \), \( a = -1 \), \( a = -2 \).
parts.answer: Four curves sharing the vertex (2, -3). The parabolas for a = 1, 2 open up (with a = 2 being narrower), while a = -1, -2 open down.

parts.stem: b) Which point do all these parabolas pass through? (Format: '(x, y)')
c) For which values of \( a \) does the parabola have \( x \)-intercepts?
d) Explain your answer to part c geometrically.
parts.answer: Geometrically, the shared vertex (2, -3) lies below the x-axis. If a > 0, the parabola opens upwards and must cross the x-axis. If a < 0, it opens downwards and moves away from the x-axis, having no intercepts.

steps.explain: Regardless of \( a \), substituting \( x = 2 \) into \( y = a(x - 2)^2 - 3 \) results in \( y = -3 \). Thus, all curves share the vertex \( (2, -3) \).

Since the vertex is below the x-axis, a parabola opening upwards (\( a > 0 \)) must cross the x-axis to extend to infinity, creating two intercepts. A parabola opening downwards (\( a < 0 \)) will extend further down and never cross it.

questions.stem: Consider the general quadratic function \( y = ax^2 + bx + c \). Complete the general completing the square derivation.

parts.stem: a) Divide through by \( a \) and complete the square in \( x \) in order to show that \( \frac{y}{a} = \left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 - \frac{b^2 - 4ac}{4a^2} \).
parts.answer: Proof: y/a = x^2 + b/a*x + c/a. Complete square: y/a = (x^2 + b/a*x + b^2/(4a^2)) + c/a - b^2/(4a^2) = (x + b/(2a))^2 - (b^2 - 4ac)/(4a^2).

parts.stem: b) Make \( y \) the subject, and hence write down the coordinates of the vertex and the equation of the axis of symmetry.
parts.answer: Vertex: (-b/(2a), -(b^2-4ac)/(4a)) or (-b/(2a), c - b^2/(4a)). Axis of symmetry: x = -b/(2a).

parts.stem: c) Put \( y = 0 \) in order to find the \( x \)-intercepts.

steps.explain: Divide by a: \( \frac{y}{a} = x^2 + \frac{b}{a}x + \frac{c}{a} \).
Add and subtract \( \left(\frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 = \frac{b^2}{4a^2} \).
Multiply by a to get \( y = a\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 - \frac{b^2 - 4ac}{4a} \). The vertex is at \( x = -\frac{b}{2a} \).

For part b, \( V(-3, -4) \) is below the x-axis, and since \( a = -2 < 0 \) it is concave down, meaning it never reaches the x-axis.
For part c, \( V(1, 0) \) lies exactly on the x-axis, meaning the vertex is the single x-intercept.

questions.stem: Complete the square for each quadratic function, and use this to write the expression in factored form.

parts.stem: a) Write \( f(x) = x^2 + 4x - 2 \) in factored form using surds. (Format: '(x + a - \sqrt{b})(x + a + \sqrt{b})')
b) Write \( f(x) = x^2 - 6x + 2 \) in factored form using surds.

steps.explain: For part a, complete the square: \( (x+2)^2 - 6 \). Use difference of squares: \( (x+2)^2 - (\sqrt{6})^2 = (x + 2 - \sqrt{6})(x + 2 + \sqrt{6}) \).
For part b, complete the square: \( (x-3)^2 - 7 \). Write in factored form: \( (x - 3 - \sqrt{7})(x - 3 + \sqrt{7}) \).
For part c, rewrite as \( 7 - (x+2)^2 = (\sqrt{7})^2 - (x+2)^2 \). Factor using difference of squares: \( (\sqrt{7} - (x+2))(\sqrt{7} + (x+2)) = (\sqrt{7} - x - 2)(\sqrt{7} + x + 2) \).

questions.stem: The general form of a quadratic with vertex \( (-3, 4) \) is \( y = a(x + 3)^2 + 4 \). Find the equation of the quadratic given these conditions.

parts.stem: a) Find the equation if the quadratic is monic. (Format: 'y = (x + h)^2 + k')
b) Find the equation if the coefficient of \( x^2 \) is 2.
c) Find the equation if the \( y \)-intercept is 22.
d) Find the equation if the curve passes through the origin. (Format: 'y = a(x + h)^2 + k' where a is a fraction)

steps.explain: For part a, monic means \( a = 1 \), so \( y = (x+3)^2 + 4 \).
For part b, coefficient of \( x^2 \) is \( a = 2 \), so \( y = 2(x+3)^2 + 4 \).
For part c, y-intercept is 22: \( 22 = a(0+3)^2 + 4 \implies 18 = 9a \implies a = 2 \), so \( y = 2(x+3)^2 + 4 \).
For part d, passes through origin \( (0, 0) \): \( 0 = a(0+3)^2 + 4 \implies 9a = -4 \implies a = -\frac{4}{9} \), so \( y = -\frac{4}{9}(x+3)^2 + 4 \).

questions.stem: Consider the parabola with equation \( y = x^2 - 4x - 1 \).

parts.stem: a) (i) Use the value of \( a \) to determine the concavity of the parabola.
a) (ii) Write down the value of the \( y \)-intercept.
a) (iii) Use the formula \( x = \frac{-b}{2a} \) to find the axis of symmetry. (Format: 'x = k')
a) (iv) Use the axis of symmetry to find the \( y \)-coordinate of the vertex.
a) (v) Calculate the discriminant \( \Delta = b^2 - 4ac \).
a) (vi) Explain why this parabola must have \( x \)-intercepts.
options: Because the vertex is below the x-axis and it is concave up.
Both of the above are correct and consistent.

parts.stem: a) (vii) Find the \( x \)-intercepts using the quadratic formula. (Format: 'x = a - \sqrt{b}, a + \sqrt{b}' in ascending order)
b) Sketch the parabola, showing these features.
parts.answer: Parabola opening upwards with vertex at (2, -5), y-intercept at (0, -1), and x-intercepts at 2 ± √5.

steps.explain: Compare the equation to the standard form \( y = ax^2 + bx + c \) to find \( a = 1, b = -4, c = -1 \). Since \( a > 0 \), the curve is concave up.
Substitute \( x = 0 \) to find the y-intercept: \( y = 0^2 - 4(0) - 1 = -1 \).
Find the axis of symmetry: \( x = \frac{-(-4)}{2(1)} = 2 \).
Substitute \( x = 2 \) to get the vertex y-coordinate: \( y = 2^2 - 4(2) - 1 = 4 - 8 - 1 = -5 \). Vertex is \( (2, -5) \).
Calculate the discriminant: \( \Delta = b^2 - 4ac = (-4)^2 - 4(1)(-1) = 16 + 4 = 20 \).
Solve \( x^2 - 4x - 1 = 0 \) using the quadratic formula: \( x = \frac{4 \pm \sqrt{20}}{2} = 2 \pm \sqrt{5} \).

Compute discriminant: \( \Delta = 36 - 8 = 28 \). Zeroes are \( x = -3 \pm \sqrt{7} \).

parts.stem: a) (ii) Write down the value of the \( y \)-intercept.

a) (vi) Explain why this parabola has no \( x \)-intercepts.
options: Because the vertex is above the x-axis \( (y = 2 > 0) \) and it is concave up.
Both of the above are correct and consistent.

parts.stem: b) Sketch the parabola, showing the \( y \)-intercept and vertex. Use symmetry to locate another point on the parabola and add this to your sketch.
parts.answer: Parabola opening upwards with vertex at (-2, 2), y-intercept at (0, 6), and symmetrical point at (-4, 6).

steps.explain: Here \( a = 1, b = 4, c = 6 \). Concavity is up because \( a > 0 \).
Substitute \( x = 0 \) to get the y-intercept of 6.
Compute the axis of symmetry: \( x = \frac{-4}{2(1)} = -2 \).
Substitute \( x = -2 \) to get the vertex y-coordinate: \( y = (-2)^2 + 4(-2) + 6 = 2 \). Vertex is \( (-2, 2) \).
Calculate the discriminant: \( \Delta = 4^2 - 4(1)(6) = 16 - 24 = -8 \).
Since \( \Delta < 0 \), there are no real roots, so there are no x-intercepts.
Use symmetry about \( x = -2 \). The y-intercept \( (0, 6) \) is 2 units to the right of the axis of symmetry. The reflection point 2 units to the left is \( (-4, 6) \).

b) Use this formula to check the coordinates of the vertices in Question 6a (\( y = x^2 + 4x + 1 \)).
parts.answer: For y = x^2 + 4x + 1: a=1, b=4, c=1. Δ = 12. x = -4/2 = -2. y = -12/4 = -3. Vertex is (-2, -3), which matches Question 6a.

steps.explain: Substitute \( x = -\frac{b}{2a} \) into \( y = ax^2 + bx + c \).

questions.stem: Let \( f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c \), where \( a \neq 0 \).

parts.stem: a) Show that \( f\left(-\frac{b}{a}\right) = f(0) \).
parts.answer: Proof: f(-b/a) = a(-b/a)^2 + b(-b/a) + c = a(b^2/a^2) - b^2/a + c = b^2/a - b^2/a + c = c. Since f(0) = c, f(-b/a) = f(0) holds.

parts.stem: b) Explain this result in terms of the symmetry of the parabola.
parts.answer: The axis of symmetry is x = -b/(2a). The points x = 0 and x = -b/a are symmetric because their midpoint is (-b/a + 0)/2 = -b/(2a), and both points lie b/(2a) units away from the axis. Thus, they must have the same y-value, which is c.

steps.explain: Evaluate the function at \( x = -\frac{b}{a} \) and \( x = 0 \).
steps.work: f\left(-\frac{b}{a}\right) = a\left(-\frac{b}{a}\right)^2 + b\left(-\frac{b}{a}\right) + c = c = f(0)

steps.explain: The midpoint of the interval \( [0, -\frac{b}{a}] \) is \( x = -\frac{b}{2a} \), which is the axis of symmetry. Symmetrical inputs always produce equal outputs.

questions.stem: Use a graphing system to compare \( y = 0.5x \), \( y = 0.5x^3 \), and \( y = 0.5x^5 \) on a single set of axes.

parts.stem: a) Which three points do all three graphs pass through? (Format: '(x1, y1), (x2, y2), (x3, y3)' in ascending x order)
b) For \( 0 < x < 1 \), which curve is nearest the \( x \)-axis?
options: They are all at the same distance

parts.stem: c) For \( x > 1 \), which curve is nearest the \( x \)-axis?
options: They are all at the same distance

parts.stem: d) For \( -1 < x < 0 \), which curve is nearest the \( x \)-axis?
options: They are all at the same distance

parts.stem: e) For \( x < -1 \), which curve is nearest the \( x \)-axis?
options: They are all at the same distance

parts.stem: f) Describe what happens when each curve is rotated by \( 180^\circ \) about the origin.
parts.answer: Each curve maps exactly onto itself under a 180-degree rotation. This occurs because the index (power of x) is odd, making these functions odd functions, symmetric about the origin: \( f(-x) = -f(x) \).

steps.explain: Common points: Since \( 1^p = 1 \), \( (-1)^p = -1 \) (for odd \( p \)), and \( 0^p = 0 \), all functions evaluate to \( \pm 0.5 \) at \( x = \pm 1 \) and \( 0 \) at \( x=0 \).

Power comparisons: For \( 0 < x < 1 \), increasing the power reduces the value (e.g. \( x^5 < x^3 < x \)), so \( 0.5x^5 \) is closest to \( y=0 \). For \( x > 1 \), higher powers are larger, so \( 0.5x \) is closest to the axis.

steps.explain: Common points: Since \( 1^p = 1 \) and \( (-1)^p = 1 \) for even \( p \), and \( 0^p = 0 \), all curves evaluate to \( 2 \) at \( x = \pm 1 \) and \( 0 \) at \( x=0 \).

questions.stem:
Sketch the graphs of these three cubic functions using technology or by plotting key points:

\( \text{(i) } y = \frac{1}{3}x^3 + 1 \)
\( \text{(ii) } y = \frac{1}{4}(x^3 - 6x^2 + 9x) \)
\( \text{(iii) } y = \frac{1}{3}(x^3 - 3x^2 - 9x + 5) \)
questions.answer: i) inflection at (0,1), ii) local max at (1, 1.125), local min at (3,0), double root at 3, iii) local max at (-1, 3.33), local min at (3, -7.33), roots at 1, 5, -2.33.

steps.explain: Evaluate key characteristics of each curve.
steps.work:
\text{(i) } y = \frac{1}{3}x^3 + 1 \text{ is a standard cubic curve shifted up by 1. Inflection point is at } (0, 1).
\text{(ii) Factored form: } y = \frac{1}{4}x(x-3)^2. \text{ x-intercepts at } x=0 \text{ (crosses) and } x=3 \text{ (touches/turning point).
(iii) Derivative: } y' = \frac{1}{3}(3x^2 - 6x - 9) = x^2 - 2x - 3 = (x-3)(x+1). \text{ Turning points at } x=-1 \text{ and } x=3.

questions.stem: On the same coordinate plane, sketch both \( y = 2\sqrt{x} \) and \( y = -2\sqrt{x} \). Describe the shape that is formed when these two curves are combined.
questions.answer: Combining the two halves forms a sideways parabola with equation y^2 = 4x opening to the right.

steps.explain: The curve \( y = 2\sqrt{x} \) represents the upper branch of a sideways opening parabola, and \( y = -2\sqrt{x} \) represents the lower branch. Combining them yields all points satisfying \( y^2 = 4x \).

questions.stem:
Analyze and graph the following cubic functions:

\( \text{(i) } c(x) = x^3 + 2x \)
\( \text{(ii) } c(x) = 2x^3 \)
\( \text{(iii) } c(x) = x^3 - 4x \)

Explain their symmetries and key shape differences.
questions.answer: All curves are odd functions (symmetric under 180 degree rotation about the origin). i) is strictly increasing with no turning points, ii) is strictly increasing with a flat inflection point at origin, iii) has two turning points and three x-intercepts (-2, 0, 2).

steps.explain: Symmetry: For all three, \( c(-x) = -c(x) \), so they are odd functions (origin symmetry).

Behavior differences: \( x^3 + 2x \) has a derivative of \( 3x^2 + 2 > 0 \), so it is strictly increasing with no stationary points. \( 2x^3 \) has derivative \( 6x^2 \), which is 0 only at the origin (flat inflection). \( x^3 - 4x \) factorizes as \( x(x-2)(x+2) \) and has stationary points where \( 3x^2 - 4 = 0 \implies x = \pm \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \).

questions.stem: The function \(f(x)\) is defined by \(f(x)=x^5-5x^3+kx\). Using your value of \(k\) from part (a), complete the following sketch of \(f(x)\).
questions.answer: With \(k=4\), factor \(f(x)=x^5-5x^3+4x=x(x^2-1)(x^2-4)=x(x-1)(x+1)(x-2)(x+2)\). The x-intercepts are \((-2,0),(-1,0),(0,0),(1,0),(2,0)\). Since the leading term is \(x^5\), the curve falls to the left and rises to the right. The function is odd, so it has rotational symmetry of 180° about the origin.
questions.hint: First use k=4, then factor f(x) completely to find all five x-intercepts. Use the positive leading term x⁵ for the end behaviour, and the odd symmetry from part (b) to shape the curve.

steps.explain: Use the value from part (a), k=4, in the function. The graph crosses the x-axis wherever f(x)=0.
Factor out x, then treat x² as a variable: x⁴−5x²+4=(x²−1)(x²−4). This gives every x-intercept.

steps.explain: Recognise the polynomial degree of \(y = x^3 + 1\). Since the highest power of \(x\) is 3, the graph is a cubic curve having a characteristic S-shape with an inflection point. This eliminates Graph A (linear line), Graph C (exponential curve), and Graph D (parabola).

steps.explain: Determine the key points of the curve:\n• \(y\)-intercept: Set \(x = 0 \implies y = 0^3 + 1 = 1\), so it crosses the \(y\)-axis at \((0, 1)\). Since \(\frac{dy}{dx} = 3x^2 = 0\) at \(x = 0\), this point is a horizontal point of inflection.\n• \(x\)-intercept: Set \(y = 0 \implies x^3 + 1 = 0 \implies x = -1\), crossing the \(x\)-axis at \((-1, 0)\).
steps.work: \(\begin{aligned} \text{y-intercept / Inflection: } & x = 0 \implies y = 1 \implies (0, 1) \\ \text{x-intercept: } & y = 0 \implies x^3 = -1 \implies x = -1 \implies (-1, 0) \end{aligned}\)

steps.explain: The graph rises at both far ends. That is the end behaviour of an even-degree polynomial with a positive leading coefficient.
steps.work: \(\text{degree is even; leading coefficient is positive}\)

steps.explain: At a and c, the curve crosses the x-axis, so those roots have odd multiplicity. At b it touches and turns back, so b is a repeated root; the squared factor represents this.
The only option with these factors and a positive leading coefficient is B.

questions.stem: The function \(y=(1-x)(x+1)(x-2)^2\) is to be graphed. Which of these is the graph of the function?
questions.solution: C
questions.hint: Find the zeros and decide whether the curve crosses or touches at each one. Also check the sign of the leading term and the y-intercept.

steps.explain: Set each factor equal to zero. The roots are −1, 1 and 2; the factor for 2 is squared.
At \(x=-1\) and \(x=1\) the factors occur once, so the curve crosses the axis. At \(x=2\) the squared factor gives an even multiplicity, so it touches and turns.
Substituting \(x=0\) gives \(y=4\). The leading term is \(-x^4\), so both ends point down. Graph B matches all these checks: crossing at \(-1\) and \(1\), touching at \(2\), \(y\)-intercept \(4\).

keyPoints.text: Which of these is the graph of the function?
keyPoints.note: Match all intercepts, multiplicities, the y-intercept and the end behaviour.

questions.stem: The circle \(x^2+(y-c)^2=r^2\), where \(c>0\) and \(r>0\), lies inside the parabola \(y=x^2\). The circle touches the parabola at exactly two points located symmetrically on opposite sides of the y-axis.

parts.stem: i) Show that \(4c=1+4r^2\).
parts.answer: Substitute \(y=x^2\) into the circle equation. The resulting quadratic in \(u=x^2\) has a repeated root at tangency, so its discriminant is zero and \(4c=1+4r^2\).
parts.hint: At a touching point both equations hold. Substitute y=x², set u=x², then use the repeated-root condition for the two tangency points.

steps.explain: At a point where the circle meets the parabola, y=x². Substitute this into the circle equation.
Let u=x². Expand the square and collect terms to form a quadratic in u.
Tangency occurs when the two intersection roots in u coincide, so the discriminant is zero.
Expand and simplify; the c² terms cancel, leaving the required relation.

parts.stem: ii) Deduce that \(c>\frac12\).
parts.answer: The repeated root is \(u=c-\frac12\). Since the two tangency points are distinct and lie on opposite sides of the y-axis, \(x^2=u>0\), so \(c>\frac12\).
parts.hint: Use the repeated root of the quadratic in u=x². Two distinct symmetric touching points require a positive value of x².

steps.explain: For a repeated root, use \(u=-\dfrac{\text{coefficient of }u}{2}\). This gives \(u=c-\dfrac12\).
The two contact points are distinct and symmetric, so their x-coordinates are nonzero. Thus u=x² is positive.
Combine \(u=c-\dfrac12\) with \(u>0\).

questions.hint: Tangency gives a repeated root after substituting y=x²; two distinct symmetric contact points make that repeated value x² positive.

questions.stem: Consider the function \( y=\dfrac{4x-3}{x} \).

parts.stem: (a) Show that \( \dfrac{4x-3}{x} = -\dfrac{3}{x}+4 \).

steps.explain: Split the single fraction \( \dfrac{4x-3}{x} \) into two separate fractions by dividing each term of the numerator by \( x \).
Simplify \( \dfrac{4x}{x} \) to 4 (cancelling the common factor of \( x \), since \( x\ne0 \)).
Reorder the terms to match the target form \( -\dfrac{3}{x}+4 \) (addition is commutative, so this is the same expression).

parts.stem: (b) Hence or otherwise, sketch the graph of \( y=\dfrac{4x-3}{x} \), showing any asymptotes and the x-intercept.
parts.answer: Vertical asymptote \( x=0 \); horizontal asymptote \( y=4 \); x-intercept \( \left(\tfrac34,0\right) \); curve approaches \( y=4 \) from below as \( x\to+\infty \) and from above as \( x\to-\infty \).

steps.explain: Find the x-intercept by setting \( f(x)=0 \). A fraction is zero when its numerator is zero.
Plot this x-intercept \( (3/4, 0) \) on the coordinate plane.

steps.explain: Sketch the hyperbola curves using the asymptotes as guides, ensuring the curve passes through the x-intercept.
Part (a): split the fraction \((4x-3)/x\) into two separate fractions over the same denominator, one for each term of the numerator.
Rearrange the two terms into the exact form requested by the question.
Part (b): use the rewritten form to identify the asymptotes. The function \(y = -\dfrac{3}{x} + 4\) is a transformation of \(y = \dfrac{1}{x}\): reflected, scaled by 3, and shifted up 4.
steps.work: Vertical asymptote: \(x = 0\) (denominator cannot be zero).\\ Horizontal asymptote: \(y = 4\) (as \(x \to \pm\infty\), \(-\dfrac{3}{x} \to 0\)).

steps.explain: Find the x-intercept by setting \(y = 0\) in the original form \(\dfrac{4x-3}{x} = 0\), which requires the numerator to be zero.

Sketch the hyperbola using the two branches determined by the asymptotes \(x=0\), \(y=4\), and the x-intercept at \(\left(\dfrac{3}{4},0\right)\). Since the coefficient of \(1/x\) is \(-3\) (negative), the branch in the region \(x>0\) approaches \(y=4\) from below as \(x\to\infty\) and shoots down through the x-intercept as \(x \to 0^+\); the branch for \(x<0\) approaches \(y=4\) from above.

questions.stem: Consider the hyperbola \( y = \frac{6}{x} \).

parts.stem: a) Complete the table of values for \( y = \frac{6}{x} \) at \( x = -6, -3, -2, -1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 6 \). (Format: 'y = a, b, c, d, e, undefined, f, g, h, i, j')
b) Plot the points and sketch the hyperbola.
parts.answer: Two branches of a hyperbola: one in quadrant 1 passing through (0.5,12), (1,6), (2,3), (3,2), (6,1) and one in quadrant 3 passing through (-0.5,-12), (-1,-6), (-2,-3), (-3,-2), (-6,-1).

parts.stem: c) Which two quadrants do the branches of the curve lie in?
d) Write down the equations of the two asymptotes of the hyperbola. (Format: 'x = a, y = b')
e) State the domain and range of the function. (Format: 'domain: x != a, range: y != b')

steps.explain: Evaluate \( y = \frac{6}{x} \) for each x-value. Notice that \( x=0 \) is undefined because division by zero is impossible.
The curve consists of two separate smooth branches lying in quadrants 1 and 3.
As \( x \to \pm\infty \), \( y \to 0 \), so \( y=0 \) is a horizontal asymptote. As \( x \to 0 \), \( y \to \pm\infty \), so \( x=0 \) is a vertical asymptote.
Since the function is undefined only at \( x=0 \) and can yield any value except \( y=0 \), the domain is \( x \neq 0 \) and range is \( y \neq 0 \).

questions.stem: Construct a table of values and sketch the hyperbola \( y = -\frac{8}{x} \). Write down its domain, range, asymptotes, and which quadrants the branches lie in.
questions.answer: Branches lie in quadrants 2 and 4. Domain: x != 0, Range: y != 0. Asymptotes: x = 0, y = 0.

steps.explain: Since the numerator is negative, the branches of the hyperbola lie in quadrants 2 and 4. The vertical asymptote is \( x = 0 \) and the horizontal asymptote is \( y = 0 \).

questions.stem: Construct a table of values and sketch the hyperbola \( y = -\frac{5}{x} \). Write down its domain, range, asymptotes, and quadrants.
questions.answer: Branches lie in quadrants 2 and 4. Domain: x != 0, Range: y != 0. Asymptotes: x = 0, y = 0.

steps.explain: This hyperbola lies in quadrants 2 and 4. Its asymptotes are the axes \( x = 0 \) and \( y = 0 \).

questions.stem: Compare the hyperbolas \( y = \frac{2}{x} \), \( y = \frac{6}{x} \), and \( y = \frac{12}{x} \).

parts.stem: a) Which two quadrants do the branches of each hyperbola lie in?
b) Write down the coordinates of the points on each hyperbola closest to the origin. (Format: 'k=2: (x1, y1) and (x2, y2); k=6: ...; k=12: ...' to 2 dec places)
c) Besides \( y = x \), in which other line are the graphs of these hyperbolas symmetric?

steps.explain: Since all numerators are positive, the branches are in quadrants 1 and 3.
The point on \( y = \frac{k}{x} \) closest to the origin lies on the line of symmetry \( y = x \). Substituting \( y = x \) gives \( x^2 = k \implies x = \pm\sqrt{k} \).
steps.work:
k=2 \implies x = \pm\sqrt{2} \approx \pm 1.41
k=6 \implies x = \pm\sqrt{6} \approx \pm 2.45
k=12 \implies x = \pm\sqrt{12} \approx \pm 3.46

steps.explain: Hyperbolas of the form \( y = \frac{k}{x} \) are symmetric in both lines of symmetry \( y = x \) (which crosses the branches) and \( y = -x \) (which separates the branches).

questions.stem: Sketch the shifted exponential curve \( y = 2^x - 4 \). Identify the \( y \)-intercept, the \( x \)-intercept, the horizontal asymptote, and state the domain and range.
questions.answer: y-intercept: (0, -3), x-intercept: (2, 0), Asymptote: y = -4. Domain: all real x, Range: y > -4.

steps.explain: Substitute \( x = 0 \) to find the y-intercept: \( y = 2^0 - 4 = -3 \).
Set \( y = 0 \) to find the x-intercept: \( 2^x - 4 = 0 \implies 2^x = 4 \implies x = 2 \).
The horizontal asymptote is shifted down by 4, so it is \( y = -4 \). Range is \( y > -4 \).

questions.stem: Compare the exponential curves \( y = 1.8^x \), \( y = 2.8^x \), and \( y = 3.8^x \) on a single set of axes. Describe how the curves behave for \( x > 0 \) and \( x < 0 \).
questions.answer: For x > 0, higher bases rise faster. For x < 0, higher bases approach the asymptote y=0 faster. All pass through (0,1).

steps.explain: Since all bases are greater than 1, all curves represent exponential growth and pass through the point \( (0, 1) \).
For \( x > 0 \), \( 3.8^x > 2.8^x > 1.8^x \), so the curve with the largest base rises the steepest. For \( x < 0 \), the curve with the largest base decays to zero the fastest.

questions.stem: Sketch the exponential curve \( y = 8^x \). Identify its key features.
questions.answer: Strictly increasing curve passing through (0,1) and (1,8). Horizontal asymptote at y = 0.

steps.explain: This represents rapid exponential growth. The y-intercept is at \( (0, 1) \) and horizontal asymptote is the x-axis \( y = 0 \).

questions.stem: Sketch the exponential curve \( y = 0.25^x \). Identify its key features.
questions.answer: Strictly decreasing curve passing through (0,1) and (-1,4). Horizontal asymptote at y = 0 to the right.

steps.explain: Since the base is \( 0.25 = \frac{1}{4} = 4^{-1} < 1 \), this represents exponential decay. The curve falls from left to right.

questions.stem: Consider the functions \( y = 2^{-x} \), \( y = 5^{-x} \), and \( y = 2.5^{-x} \).

parts.stem: a) Sketch these three exponential functions on a single set of axes.
parts.answer: Three decreasing exponential curves, all passing through (0,1). The curve y = 5^-x is steepest for x < 0 and closest to the x-axis for x > 0.

parts.stem: b) How do these curves compare to the standard growth curves \( y = 2^x \) and \( y = 5^x \)?
options: They are reflections of the growth curves in the y-axis.
They are reflections of the growth curves in the x-axis.
They are shifted versions of the growth curves.
They are identical to the growth curves.

parts.stem: c) Write down the domain and range of each function. (Format: 'domain: ..., range: ...')
parts.answer: domain: all real x, range: y > 0

steps.explain: Since \( a^{-x} = (a^{-1})^x = (\frac{1}{a})^x \), these represent exponential decay.
Replacing \( x \) with \( -x \) in any function \( f(x) \) reflects its graph horizontally across the y-axis.

questions.stem: Sketch the exponential graph \( y = 6^x \) without using a table of values. Make sure the y-intercept and one other reference point are clearly marked.
questions.answer: Graph rising to the right, passing through (0,1) and (1,6). Horizontal asymptote at y = 0.

steps.explain: Locate the y-intercept: \( f(0) = 6^0 = 1 \). Find another reference point: \( f(1) = 6^1 = 6 \). Draw the growth curve heading towards the x-axis on the left.

questions.stem: Sketch the exponential graph \( y = 3^{-x} \) without using a table of values.
questions.answer: Graph falling to the right, passing through (0,1) and (-1,3). Horizontal asymptote at y = 0 on the right.

steps.explain: Y-intercept is \( (0,1) \). Another point is \( x = -1 \implies y = 3 \). Since the exponent has a negative sign, the graph decays to the right.

questions.stem: Does the equation \( x^2 - y^2 = 0 \) represent a hyperbola? Justify your choice.
options: No, because it factorizes into \( (x-y)(x+y) = 0 \), which represents two intersecting straight lines.
Yes, it is a standard rectangular hyperbola centered at the origin.
Yes, it is a hyperbola with asymptotes \( y = \pm x \) but has no real vertices.
No, it represents a circle of radius 0.

steps.explain: Factorize the difference of two squares.
This yields two linear equations: \( y = x \) or \( y = -x \). This is a pair of intersecting lines, not a hyperbola (it is a degenerate hyperbola).

questions.stem: Consider the function \( y = \left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^x \).

parts.stem: a) Construct a table of values and sketch the graph.
parts.answer: Symmetric decaying curve passing through (0,1), (1, 1/3), (-1, 3), and (-2, 9).

parts.stem: b) Use the index laws to explain why \( y = \left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^x \) has the exact same graph as \( y = 3^{-x} \).
parts.answer: Proof: By definition, 1/3 = 3^-1. Using the power of a power rule: (1/3)^x = (3^-1)^x = 3^(-1*x) = 3^-x. Thus the functions are identical.

steps.explain: Rewrite the fraction using a negative index.

questions.stem: Let \(f(x)=\frac{x}{x-1}\).

parts.stem: i) Show \(\frac{x}{x-1}=1+\frac{1}{x-1}\).
parts.hint: Rewrite 1 with denominator x−1, then combine the two fractions.

steps.explain: The denominator x−1 cannot be zero, so this identity is considered for x≠1.
Write 1 as a fraction whose denominator is x−1.
Add the numerators over the common denominator.

parts.stem: ii) Hence, or otherwise, on the same number plane, draw sketches of \(y=\frac{x}{x-1}\) and \(y=\frac{1}{x-1}\).
parts.answer: Both curves have vertical asymptote \(x=1\). The first has horizontal asymptote \(y=1\) and passes through \((0,0)\); the second has horizontal asymptote \(y=0\) and passes through \((0,-1)\).
parts.hint: Use the rearrangements to identify each horizontal asymptote. Both denominators are zero at \(x=1\), giving the common vertical asymptote.

steps.explain: For \(\dfrac{x}{x-1}\), use \(\dfrac{x}{x-1}=1+\dfrac{1}{x-1}\). The reciprocal term tends to zero far from \(x=1\), so the horizontal asymptote is \(y=1\). It also passes through \((0,0)\).

For \(\dfrac{1}{x-1}\), the numerator is \(1\) and the fraction tends to zero for large \(|x|\). Its horizontal asymptote is \(y=0\); substituting \(x=0\) gives the point \((0,-1)\). The overlay below shows both curves on the same axes.

questions.hint: For the algebra, make a common denominator. For the graphs, find the shared vertical asymptote and each horizontal asymptote.

questions.stem:
i) Verify that \(x=\frac13\) and \(x=2\) satisfy the equation \(7-3x=\frac2x\).
ii) On the same set of axes, sketch the graphs of \(y=7-3x\) and \(y=\frac2x\).
iii) Using part ii, or otherwise, write down all values of x for which \(7-3x<\frac2x\).

parts.stem: i) Verify that \(x=\frac13\) and \(x=2\) satisfy the equation \(7-3x=\frac2x\).
parts.answer: For x=1/3, both sides equal 6. For x=2, both sides equal 1.
parts.hint: Substitute each value into the left-hand side and right-hand side separately.

steps.explain: Substitute \(x=\dfrac13\) into each side.
Now substitute \(x=2\) into each side.
Each pair of values agrees, so both numbers satisfy the equation.

parts.stem: ii) On the same set of axes, sketch the graphs of \(y=7-3x\) and \(y=\frac2x\).
parts.answer: A decreasing line and the rectangular hyperbola y=2/x intersecting at (1/3,6) and (2,1).
parts.hint: For the line, use its y-intercept and gradient. For the hyperbola, use its two asymptotes and the intersection points verified in part i.

steps.explain: The line has \(y\)-intercept \(7\) and gradient \(-3\). The reciprocal curve has asymptotes \(x=0\) and \(y=0\).
Plot the two verified intersections from part i and sketch both curves through them.

parts.stem: iii) Using part ii, or otherwise, write down all values of x for which \(7-3x<\frac2x\).
parts.hint: Read where the line is below the reciprocal curve. Keep \(x=0\) excluded because \(\dfrac2x\) is undefined.

steps.explain: Bring the expressions together over the common denominator x. Remember x cannot be 0.
Factor the numerator using its roots \(\dfrac13\) and \(2\).
Check signs on the intervals separated by \(0\), \(\dfrac13\) and \(2\). Testing one \(x\)-value in each interval shows negativity on \(\left(0,\dfrac13\right)\) and \((2,\infty)\).

questions.hint: Use the line and hyperbola to see where the line lies below the curve.

questions.stem: The time it takes for a cupcake at a picnic to be eaten by ants (\(t\) minutes) varies inversely with the number of ants eating the cupcake (\(N\) ants). When there are 10 ants the cupcake is eaten in 120 minutes. The equation relating \(t\) and \(N\) is \(t = \frac{k}{N}\). What is the value of \(k\)?

steps.explain: Substitute the given pair of values, \(N=10\) and \(t=120\), into the equation.
Multiply both sides by 10 to isolate \(k\).

meta.source: Hills Grammar 2025 2U Trials

questions.stem: By first completing the table of values, graph the curve \(t = \frac{1200}{N}\) representing the relationship between the time taken for the cupcake to be eaten and the number of ants eating the cupcake, from \(N=10\) to \(N=120\).

steps.explain: Use \(t=\frac{1200}{N}\) (with \(k=1200\) from part (a)) to complete the table for each given value of \(N\).
Plot all four points \((N,t)\) on the given axes and join them with a smooth curve — this is the characteristic inverse-variation (hyperbola) shape, decreasing steeply at first then levelling off.

questions.stem: Consider a situation where \( y \) varies directly with \( x \).

parts.stem: a) Write this relationship algebraically using \( k \) as the constant of proportionality.
b) Find the value of \( k \) if \( y = 12 \) when \( x = 3 \).
c) Find the value of \( k \) if \( y = -10 \) when \( x = 2 \).
d) Find the value of \( k \) if \( y = 8 \) when \( x = 5 \).

steps.explain: If \( y \) varies directly with \( x \), the algebraic relationship is of the form \( y = kx \).
Substitute the given values to solve for \( k \).
steps.work:
12 = k \cdot 3 \implies k = 4
-10 = k \cdot 2 \implies k = -5
8 = k \cdot 5 \implies k = 1.6

questions.stem: It is known that \( y \) is inversely proportional to \( x \). If the algebraic relation is written as \( y = \frac{k}{x} \), find the value of the constant of proportionality \( k \) when \( y = 3 \) and \( x = 4 \).

steps.explain: Substitute \( y = 3 \) and \( x = 4 \) into the inverse variation equation \( y = \frac{k}{x} \).

questions.stem: It is known that \( y \) is inversely proportional to \( x \). If the algebraic relation is written as \( y = \frac{k}{x} \), find the value of the constant of proportionality \( k \) when \( y = \frac{1}{4} \) and \( x = -2 \).

steps.explain: Substitute \( y = \frac{1}{4} \) and \( x = -2 \) into the inverse variation equation \( y = \frac{k}{x} \).

questions.stem: It is known that \( y \) is inversely proportional to \( x \). If the algebraic relation is written as \( y = \frac{k}{x} \), find the value of the constant of proportionality \( k \) when \( y = -3 \) and \( x = 5 \).

steps.explain: Substitute \( y = -3 \) and \( x = 5 \) into the inverse variation equation \( y = \frac{k}{x} \).

questions.stem: Investigate what happens to the variables under direct and inverse variation.

parts.stem: a) i) If the value of \( y \) varies directly with \( x \), what happens to the value of \( y \) when the value of \( x \) is tripled?
a) ii) If the value of \( y \) varies directly with \( x \), what happens to the value of \( y \) when the value of \( x \) is divided by 4?
b) i) If the value of \( y \) varies inversely with \( x \), what happens to the value of \( y \) when the value of \( x \) is tripled?
b) ii) If the value of \( y \) varies inversely with \( x \), what happens to the value of \( y \) when the value of \( x \) is divided by 4?

steps.explain: For direct variation \( y = kx \), any scale factor applied to \( x \) is directly multiplied to \( y \).
For inverse variation \( y = \frac{k}{x} \), any scale factor applied to \( x \) acts inversely on \( y \).

questions.stem: The quantity \( y \) varies inversely with the square of \( x \).

parts.stem: a) i) Write this relationship algebraically using \( k \) as the constant of proportionality.
a) ii) Determine the constant \( k \) if it is found that \( y = 3 \) when \( x = 2 \).
a) iii) Evaluate \( y \) when \( x = 4 \).
b) i) What happens to the value of \( y \) when the value of \( x \) is tripled?
b) ii) What happens to the value of \( y \) when the value of \( x \) is divided by 4?

steps.explain: The phrase 'varies inversely with the square of x' translates to \( y = \frac{k}{x^2} \).
Substitute \( y = 3 \) and \( x = 2 \) to find \( k \).
Substitute \( k = 12 \) and \( x = 4 \) to find \( y \).
Since \( y \propto \frac{1}{x^2} \), tripling \( x \) results in dividing \( y \) by \( 3^2 = 9 \). Dividing \( x \) by 4 results in multiplying \( y \) by \( 4^2 = 16 \).

questions.stem: The area \( A\text{ cm}^2 \) of a triangle varies directly with its height \( h\text{ cm} \).

parts.stem: a) Write this algebraically using \( k \) as the constant of proportionality.
b) Determine \( k \) if \( A = 15\text{ cm}^2 \) when \( h = 5\text{ cm} \).
c) What are the units of \( k \)?
d) Explain the units of \( k \) using the formula for the area of a triangle.
parts.answer: The formula for the area of a triangle is \( A = \frac{1}{2}bh \). Comparing this to \( A = kh \) shows that \( k = \frac{1}{2}b \), where \( b \) is the base of the triangle. Since \( b \) is a length measured in cm, the constant of proportionality \( k \) represents half the base length and must also have units of cm.

steps.explain: Since area varies directly with height, the relationship is \( A = kh \).
Substitute \( A = 15 \) and \( h = 5 \) to find \( k \).
Rearrange to solve for the units of \( k \).

questions.stem: In a scale model of a Mustang (aeroplane), each length \( m \) on the model varies directly with the corresponding length \( s \) on the Mustang.

parts.stem: a) Write this algebraically using \( k \) as the constant of proportionality.
b) The length of the Mustang is \( 10.0\text{ m} \) and the model has length \( 0.25\text{ m} \). What is the constant of proportionality \( k \)?
c) The height of the Mustang on the runway is \( 3.6\text{ m} \). What is the height of the model in cm?
d) The wingspan of the model is \( 285\text{ mm} \). What is the wingspan of the Mustang in metres?

steps.explain: Write the direct variation relation.
Substitute \( s = 10.0 \) and \( m = 0.25 \) to find \( k \).
Find model height using \( k = 0.025 \) and \( s = 3.6\text{ m} \).
Convert model wingspan to metres and find Mustang wingspan.

questions.stem: The amount of paint \( P \), in litres, used to paint a building is directly proportional to the area \( A \), in square metres, to be covered.

parts.stem: a) Write this algebraically using \( k \) as the constant of proportionality.
b) A certain building requires \( 36\text{ L} ) to cover an area of \( 360\text{ m}^2 \). Find the constant of proportionality \( k \).
c) A larger building has an area of \( 452\text{ m}^2  \) to be painted. How many litres of paint will this require?

d) A paint supplier sells \( 20\text{ L}  \) buckets and \( 2\text{ L}  \) tins of paint. What is the minimum number of buckets and tins that must be bought to cover the \( 452\text{ m}^2  \) area completely with zero or minimal leftover? (Format: 'X buckets and Y tins')

steps.explain: Since paint varies directly with area, \( P = kA \).
Find \( k \) by substituting \( P = 36 \) and \( A = 360 \).
Find paint required for \( A = 452 \).
Determine the combination of 20 L buckets and 2 L tins that sums to exactly 45.2 L or slightly more.
steps.work: 2 \text{ buckets} = 40\text{ L}. \text{ Remaining } 5.2\text{ L} \implies 3 \text{ tins} = 6\text{ L}. \text{ Total } = 46\text{ L}.

questions.stem: For an ideal gas, the relationships between pressure \( P \), volume \( V \), and temperature \( T \) are modeled by direct and inverse variation.

parts.stem: a) i) If kept at constant pressure, volume \( V \) varies directly with temperature \( T \) (in Kelvin). Write this relationship using constant \( k \).
a) ii) A gas occupies \( 1.5\text{ m}^3  \) when \( T = 300\text{ K} \). What volume in \( \text{cm}^3 \) will it occupy when the temperature is \( T = 320\text{ K} \)?
b) i) If kept at constant temperature, pressure \( P \) varies inversely with volume \( V \). Write this relationship using constant \( k \).

b) ii) A certain amount of gas is at \( 3 \) times atmospheric pressure when it occupies \( 8\text{ L} \). What is the pressure when the volume is \( 20\text{ L} \)? (Express as a multiple of atmospheric pressure)

steps.explain: Set up the direct variation relation for volume and temperature.
Find \( k \) and calculate volume at \( T = 320\text{ K} \). Convert \( \text{m}^3 \) to \( \text{cm}^3 \).
Set up the inverse variation relation for pressure and volume.
Find \( k \) and calculate pressure at \( V = 20\text{ L} \).

questions.stem: An object starts from rest and accelerates with constant acceleration.

parts.stem: a) i) If velocity \( v\text{ m/s} \) varies directly with time \( t\text{ s} \), and after \( 3\text{ s} \) the speed is \( 6\text{ m/s} \), find the constant of proportionality \( k \).
a) ii) What is the speed of the object at \( t = 10\text{ s} \)?
a) iii) When will the object be travelling at \( 15\text{ m/s} \)?
b) Write the formula for distance \( x \) being proportional to the square of time \( t  \) algebraically using \( k \) as the constant of proportionality.
c) i) If after \( 3\text{ s} \) the distance travelled is \( x = 9\text{ m} \), find the value of the constant of proportionality \( k \).
c) ii) How far has the object travelled at \( t = 10\text{ s} \)?
c) iii) How much time has elapsed when \( x = 144\text{ m} \)?
c) iv) What happens to the distance \( x \) when the value of \( t \) is doubled?

steps.explain: Velocity varies directly with time: \( v = kt \). Use \( v(3) = 6 \) to find \( k = 2 \).
Find speed at \( t = 10 \) and time at \( v = 15 \).
Distance is proportional to the square of time: \( x = kt^2 \). Use \( x(3) = 9 \) to find \( k = 1 \).
Find distance at \( t = 10 \) and time at \( x = 144 \).
Since \( x \propto t^2 \), doubling \( t  \) results in multiplying \( x \) by \( 2^2 = 4 \).

questions.stem: The acceleration \( a \) due to gravity on Mars varies inversely with the square of the distance \( r \) to the centre of Mars.

parts.stem: a) Write this algebraically using \( k \) as the constant of proportionality.

b) At the surface of Mars, the acceleration due to gravity is approximately \( 3.71\text{ m/s}^2 \) and the radius is \( 3,389,500\text{ m} \). Find the value of \( k \) correct to 3 significant figures.
c) A ball is dropped from a tower \( 60\text{ m} \) above Mars surface. Show that the acceleration due to gravity at this height is still \( 3.71\text{ m/s}^2 \) correct to two decimal places.
parts.answer: Substituting \( r = 3,389,500 + 60 = 3,389,560\text{ m} \) into the formula: \( a = \frac{4.26 \times 10^{13}}{3,389,560^2} \approx 3.71\text{ m/s}^2 \). The difference is negligible at this scale.

parts.stem: d) A satellite is in orbit around Mars at an altitude of \( 17,000\text{ km} \) above the surface. Find the acceleration due to gravity at this height, correct to 2 decimal places. (in \( \text{m/s}^2 \))
e) What happens to \( a  \) when the distance from the centre of Mars is doubled?

steps.explain: Mars gravity varies inversely with the square of the distance: \( a = \frac{k}{r^2} \).
Solve for \( k \) using surface gravity and radius.
Calculate gravity at altitude \( 17,000\text{ km} \) (which is \( 1.7 \cdot 10^7\text{ m} \)).
By inverse square law, doubling distance divides gravity by \( 2^2 = 4 \).

questions.stem: The formula for simple interest is \( I = nPR \).

parts.stem: a) Suppose that interest rate \( R \) and number of years \( n \) are fixed. What is the relationship between \( I \) and \( P \)?
options: I is directly proportional to P
I is inversely proportional to P
I is proportional to the square of P

parts.stem: b) Suppose that interest \( I \) and principal \( P \) are fixed. What is the relationship between \( n \) and \( R \)?
options: n is inversely proportional to R
n is directly proportional to R
n is proportional to the square of R

parts.stem: c) Suppose that \( PR = k \) is constant so that \( I = kn \). What are the units of \( k \)?

steps.explain: If \( R \) and \( n \) are constant, \( I = c \cdot P \) where \( c = nR \). Thus \( I \propto P \).
If \( I \) and \( P \) are constant, \( nR = c \implies n = \frac{c}{R} \). Thus \( n \propto \frac{1}{R} \).
Since \( I = kn \) where \( I \) is in dollars and \( n \) is in years, \( k = \frac{I}{n} \) has units of dollars per year.

questions.stem: The time \( t \) taken for a tank to empty is proportional to a power of the initial depth \( h \).

parts.stem: a) i) The time to empty a cylindrical tank is proportional to the square-root of the initial depth. Write this relationship using constant \( k \).
a) ii) When the initial depth was \( 4\text{ m} \) the time taken was \( 6000\text{ s} \). How long will it take to empty this tank if it is filled to a depth of \( 9\text{ m} \)? (in seconds)
b) i) The time to empty a conical tank is proportional to the square-root of the fifth power of the initial depth. Write this relationship using constant \( k \).

b) ii) When the initial depth was \( 3\text{ m} \) the time taken was \( 486\text{ s} \). How long will it take to empty this tank if it is filled to a depth of \( 5\text{ m} \)? (Round to the nearest second)

steps.explain: Cylinder: \( t = k\sqrt{h} \). Find \( k \) and solve for \( h = 9 \).
Cone: \( t = k\sqrt{h^5} \). Find \( k \) and solve for \( h = 5 \).

questions.stem: The lateral force \( F \) required to keep a car on a bend of constant radius is proportional to the square of its speed \( V \).

parts.stem: a) Write this algebraically using \( k \) as the constant of proportionality.

b) A car drives at \( 252\text{ km/h} \) (which is \( 70\text{ m/s} \)) around a bend. The force keeping the car on the road is \( 9,800\text{ N} \). Find \( k \) when speed is measured in \( \text{m/s} \).
c) On the next lap, the car takes the corner at \( 216\text{ km/h} \) (which is \( 60\text{ m/s} \)). What is the force for this lap in newtons?
d) If the speed of the car is doubled, by what factor has the force increased?

steps.explain: The relationship is \( F = kV^2 \).
Convert speed to \( \text{m/s} \) and solve for \( k \).
Calculate force at new speed \( 60\text{ m/s} \).
Since \( F \propto V^2 \), doubling \( V \) multiplies \( F \) by \( 2^2 = 4 \).

questions.stem: For a conical pendulum, the period of oscillation \( P \) varies directly with the square-root of its length \( L \).

parts.stem: a) Write this relationship algebraically using \( k \) as the constant of proportionality.
b) When the length of the pendulum is \( L = 0.36\text{ m} \), the period is \( P = 1.20\text{ s} \). What will be the period of a conical pendulum with length \( L = 2.25\text{ m} \)? (in seconds)

steps.explain: Set up relationship: \( P = k\sqrt{L} \). Find \( k \).
Calculate period for \( L = 2.25\text{ m} \).

questions.stem: An architect is designing a building. The client has insisted that one of the rooms in the building must have an area of \( 60\text{ m}^2 \). For ease of design, the length \( \ell \) and the breadth \( b \) must each be a whole number of metres. Because of the furniture that must go into the room, no wall may be less than \( 5\text{ m} \). What are the possible dimensions of the room?
options: 5 m by 12 m, or 6 m by 10 m
4 m by 15 m, or 5 m by 12 m
6 m by 10 m, or 8 m by 7.5 m
5 m by 12 m, or 6 m by 10 m, or 4 m by 15 m

steps.explain: The area is \( A = \ell \cdot b = 60 \). Length and breadth must be positive integers.
List all integer factor pairs of 60.
Apply the constraint that no wall can be less than 5 m. This excludes pairs where any dimension is less than 5.

questions.hint: Direct variation with the cube means \(C=kh^3\). Use the first box to find \(k\), then substitute \(h=12\).

steps.explain: Write the direct-variation model.
Use the known box to find \(k\).
Substitute the new height.
Calculate the cost.

questions.stem: The weight of an object on the moon varies directly with its weight on Earth. An astronaut who weighs \(84\) kg on Earth weighs only \(14\) kg on the moon. A lunar landing craft weighs \(2449\) kg when on the moon. Calculate the weight of this landing craft when on Earth.
questions.hint: The Moon weight is proportional to Earth weight. Find the factor \(k\) from the astronaut, then solve for Earth weight.

steps.explain: Let moon weight M=k times Earth weight E. Use the astronaut data.
Use the same relationship for the lander.
Multiply both sides by 6.
Calculate and include the unit.

Substitute 40 mm.

steps.explain: The factors for these roots are \((x + 1)\) and \((x - 2)^3\) (or \((2 - x)^3\)), giving an overall polynomial degree of \(1 + 3 = 4\) (quartic). Because both ends of the graph plunge downwards towards \(-\infty\) as \(x \to \pm\infty\), the leading coefficient must be negative.
Verify the \(y\)-intercept: when \(x = 0\), \(y = (0 + 1)(2 - 0)^3 = 8 > 0\), which matches the positive \(y\)-intercept on the graph. Hence, the correct equation is Option C.

questions.stem: Logan’s dentist determined the number of cavities in his patient’s mouth each year is inversely proportional to the total number of seconds spent brushing during each session. Logan developed 6 cavities during the year in which he spent 20 seconds brushing each time. How many cavities will Logan develop annually if he increases his brushing time to a minute each time?
questions.hint: Inverse variation means cavities × brushing seconds stays constant. Convert one minute to 60 seconds.

steps.explain: Let c be cavities and t be seconds brushed. Inverse variation gives c=k/t.
Use the first year to find k.
One minute is 60 seconds. Substitute t=60.
State the annual number.

questions.stem: Sketch the graph of \(y=|x+4|\).
questions.answer: A V-shaped graph with vertex at \((-4, 0)\), \(y\)-intercept at \((0, 4)\), and branches \(y = x + 4\) for \(x \ge -4\) and \(y = -x - 4\) for \(x < -4\).
questions.hint: Set the expression inside the absolute value brackets to zero (x + 4 = 0) to locate the vertex at (-4, 0). Then find the y-intercept by substituting x = 0 to get (0, 4), and draw two symmetric rays with slopes ±1.

steps.explain: Find the vertex (turning point) of the absolute value function. The vertex of \(y = |f(x)|\) occurs where the expression inside the absolute value brackets equals zero.

steps.explain: Define the two linear branches algebraically and draw the complete V-shaped graph passing through the calculated points.
steps.work:
y = |x + 4| = \begin{cases} x + 4, & x \ge -4 \quad (\text{slope } m = 1) \\ -(x + 4) = -x - 4, & x < -4 \quad (\text{slope } m = -1) \end{cases}
\text{Draw straight rays from the vertex } (-4, 0) \text{ through } (0, 4) \text{ and } (-8, 4).

questions.hint: Geometrically, \(|x - 1| \ge 3\) means the distance between x and 1 on the number line is at least 3. Move 3 units left (to -2) and 3 units right (to 4), using solid filled dots because equality is included.

steps.explain: Interpret \(|x - 1| \ge 3\) algebraically and geometrically. The expression states that the distance from \(x\) to \(1\) on the number line is at least \(3\) units. Split this into two outside cases.
Solve each linear inequality for \(x\) by adding \(1\) to both sides.

Graph the solution set on the real number line. Because the inequality is non-strict (\(\ge\)), use solid (closed) circles at \(x = -2\) and \(x = 4\) to show they are included. Draw bold rays with arrows extending outwards to \(-\infty\) and \(+\infty\).

keyPoints.text: Solve \(|x-1|\geq3\) and graph your solution on the number line.
keyPoints.note: A distance from 1 of at least 3 means x is 3 or more units to either side of 1.

questions.stem: Sketch the graph of \(y=\sqrt{4-x^2}\), and state the range.
questions.answer: Upper semicircle of radius 2 centred at the origin \((0, 0)\), passing through \((-2, 0)\), \((0, 2)\), and \((2, 0)\); range: \([0, 2]\) (or \(0 \le y \le 2\)).
questions.hint: Square both sides to get \(x^2 + y^2 = 4\), which is a circle of radius 2 centred at the origin. Since the square root symbol denotes the principal (non-negative) root, \(y \ge 0\), the graph is the upper semicircle with range \([0, 2]\).

steps.explain: Square both sides and rearrange to identify the underlying circle equation.

questions.stem: Assume that the surface area \(S\) of a human satisfies the equation \(S=kM^{2/3}\), where \(M\) is body mass in kilograms and \(k\) is a constant of proportionality. A human with body mass 70 kg has surface area 18600 cm². Find the value of k, and hence find the surface area of a human with body mass 60 kg.
questions.hint: Substitute the known body mass and surface area to find k. For the second body mass, use S proportional to M^(2/3).

questions.stem: The time (t) taken to clean a house varies inversely with the number (n) of people cleaning the house. Which graph represents this relationship?
questions.hint: Inverse variation has the form t=k/n. Since n counts people, use positive whole-number values; as n grows, t decreases quickly at first and then levels off.

steps.explain: Translate “varies inversely” into an equation.
As n increases, t decreases. The decrease is not by equal amounts, so the graph bends and flattens rather than forming a straight line.
The number of people must be positive whole numbers. Choose the discrete curved graph, Graph A.
